title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Glaze & Grout. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Glaze & Grout
options.lineage: glazed wall tile, terrazzo floors and chrome fixtures shared by every studio
options.thesis: The page is built like the shop's wall: one glazed-tile module, one grout line, one brand glaze color.
options.viewport: The shop name set large across a wall of glazed tiles, one tile cut out as the live 'next open slot' with a chrome Book button.
options.risk: If the tile grid loosens anywhere it reads as a checkerboard gimmick instead of architecture.

raised.raise: Every graphic, image crop and gap is drawn from the same tile cell; the module is sacred.
Total palette commitment: glaze, grout, chrome, ink. Nothing else enters.
The brightest element on any screen is always the Book action, nothing competes with it.
One grout weight rules every rule, border and divider on the page.

options.label: The Appointment Book
options.lineage: the paper day-book on the front desk, time slots ruled in pencil
options.thesis: The page is today's page of the book: open slots are the hero, services are the ledger.
options.viewport: A ruled day-grid of time slots with the next open ones inked in the brand color, Book beside them.
options.risk: Closest to where most runs land; paper grounds drift toward the cream-and-serif default.

options.label: Session Sleeve
options.thesis: Every shop gets a record-sleeve: a duotone portrait cropped hard, one flat field of brand color, the name in tight caps at an angle.
options.viewport: A hard-cropped duotone portrait in one corner, a full flat brand-color band carrying the shop name and Book.
options.case: Strong audience identification with barbers and stylists; depends heavily on each shop supplying good photography.
options.risk: Nail salons and studios without portrait-grade photos will look empty.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Services as numbered pages on a 40-column grid.
options.viewport: P100 index page listing services and times.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty to a salon client.
options.case: Loses both axes: clients don't identify with broadcast teletext.
options.kept: The sacred cell: every graphic drawn from one module.

options.label: Risograph Flyer
options.thesis: The shop as a two-ink riso flyer.
options.risk: Paper ground slides into the cream default; too indie for most shops.
options.case: Loses both axes: a flyer is a one-off, not a trusted place.
options.kept: Total palette commitment to a few spot colors.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.thesis: Proximity glow as the attention model.
options.viewport: Dark ground, Book blooming to light on approach.
options.risk: Sci-fi mood has nothing to do with personal care.
options.kept: The brightest light is reserved for the focused action.

options.label: Rubber-Hose Cel
options.thesis: The shop as a bouncing cartoon gag.
options.viewport: Iris opening onto the shop name.
options.risk: Undercuts trust in the shop's craft.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.thesis: A descent as the page's axis.
options.risk: No relation to the visitor's task.
options.case: Loses both axes. Note: 5 challengers dealt; 3 strongest shown in full, rest here.
options.kept: One axis rules every line of copy.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The salon template everyone ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Dark full-bleed shop photo, centered name, Book Now button, services grid below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other shop's site by design.
